$comment: Pinned competitor set for the Tier-2 conversion matrix (bench-strategy §3, §6b F9).
Every sha256 here was computed by downloading the artifact, not copied from a page.
The harness hard-fails when an installed tool's --version disagrees with `version`:
a matrix is only comparable if the reader knows exactly what produced it, and the
lane's existing numbers rot precisely because nobody pins.
`flags_disclosed` is the full argument list the harness passes in that mode. It is a
field rather than a comment because serd's -f trap (fast-and-loose URI mode, which is
how serdi's published-looking numbers were obtained) is exactly the kind of flag that

riot.name: Apache Jena riot
riot.runtime_requirement: JDK 21+ (Jena 6.x). Hard requirement, not advisory: 6.1.0 will not start on 11 or 17.

default.note: riot's DEFAULT is check-on for Turtle and check-off for N-Triples. Recording this mode alone would compare a validating Turtle run against a non-validating N-Triples one — see §6b F3.

check_false.note: Uniform no-validation. Comparable with our --nocheck column. NOTE: Jena 6.x takes bare --check/--nocheck; the 5.x --check=BOOL spelling makes riot read the value as a FILENAME and fail, which is how this was caught.

check_true.note: Uniform validation. Becomes the primary cell once our --nocheck/validate split exists.

jvm.note: Pinned and disclosed per §6b F7. An unpinned JVM heap makes the peak-RSS column meaningless, and the memory-stability claim is restricted to -Xmx-pinned or non-JVM tools for exactly this reason.

serdi.name: serd (serdi)
serdi.install_cmd: tar -xJf serd-0.32.10.tar.xz && cd serd-0.32.10 && meson setup build && ninja -C build && ln -sf $PWD/build/serdi ../bin/serdi

default.note: Default URI handling: full resolution. This is the honest comparison cell.

fast_lax.note: THE TRAP (§3). -f is fast-and-loose URI mode. serd's own published-looking throughput was measured this way; a matrix that quotes -f numbers against another tool's validating numbers is not a comparison. Recorded so the difference is visible, never used as the headline cell.

default.note: The live Rust competitor — the most directly comparable column we have. NOTE: 0.5.x renamed the input flag to --from-file; the 0.4.x --file spelling is rejected outright, which is how this was caught.

rapper.name: raptor2 (rapper)
rapper.install_cmd: tar -xzf raptor2-2.0.16.tar.gz && cd raptor2-2.0.16 && ./configure --prefix=$PWD/../.. && make && make install
rapper.status_note: Last release 2014, last commit 2023. Carried for historical continuity with the two most-cited benchmarks in the lane — the ones that disagree about this very library by ~6x. Labelled dormant in every rendered matrix so no reader mistakes it for a live competitor.

default.note: rapper needs -i to be told the input syntax; the harness passes it per corpus.

rdflib.name: RDFLib (Python)
rdflib.sha256_note: Not pinned by hash: this is a REFERENCE row, never a competitor cell. It exists to sanity-check our output by an independent implementation (isomorphism spot-check), not to be raced.

default.note: Orders of magnitude slower than every compiled tool. Quoting it as a speed win would be dishonest framing, so it is excluded from speed cells by construction.

n3js.name: N3.js (Node)
n3js.sha256_note: Reference row, as rdflib. Pin the hash before any published run.

default.note: Ecosystem reference point for the JSON-LD/JS lane, not a competitor cell.

Our parser performs NO IRI validation today (fluree-vocab has only is_absolute_iri + resolve_iri). This cell is therefore comparable with riot's check_false, NOT with its default. Stated in the matrix rather than left for a reader to discover.

validate.note: DESIGNED NOW, FILLED LATER. When W-h8 lands, this becomes the primary cell opposite riot's check_true, and `default` gains --nocheck as the disclosed secondary. The matrix carries the column already so the comparison is never quietly asymmetric in the meantime.
